logos.main.name: Main logo
logos.main.text: The Vexl wordmark. Use it in most places.
logos.symbol.name: Symbol
logos.symbol.text: The Vexl glasses can stand on their own where people already know Vexl. The website uses the one-color glasses, the app icon the two-tone ones.
logos.secondary.name: Secondary logo
logos.secondary.text: The glasses and the wordmark side by side, for wide spaces.
logos.appIcon.name: App icon
logos.appIcon.text: The icon people see on their home screen. Use it as it is, without a frame or a shadow.
logos.space.title: Clear space
logos.space.text: Keep other logos, text, images, and page edges away from the logo. Leave free space around it about as tall as the letter v in the wordmark, or the lenses of the glasses. The files already include this space, so place them as they are.
logos.avoid.title: Things to avoid
logos.avoid.recolor: Don't use colors other than black, white, and Vexl yellow
logos.avoid.deform: Don't stretch the logo or change its proportions
logos.contrast.title: Logo on a colored background
logos.contrast.text: Use the black logo on light colors: white, yellow, light green, and light pink. Use the white or yellow logo on black and dark green.
colors.main.title: Main colors
colors.main.text: Yellow, black, and white carry the brand.
colors.secondary.title: Secondary colors
colors.secondary.text: Light and dark pairs from the app. There, the light shade is a background and the dark shade is the text on it. Almost black is the lit half of the glasses.
colors.downloads.title: Color modes
colors.downloads.text: HEX and RGB are for screens, CMYK and Pantone for print. Only the colors that list them have print values so far.
typography.downloadText: Download the whole family, or a single style and format.
typography.monument.text: Monument Extended sets headings in sentence case, never in all caps. The website sets its headings in Bold 700. The app sets its headings in Regular 400 and uses Bold 700 for short emphasized labels.
typography.satoshi.text: TT Satoshi sets everything people read: paragraphs, buttons, and labels. Use Medium 500 for text and DemiBold 600 for emphasis.

people.viliam.bio: Viliam Klamarčík took over as CEO of Vexl in November 2025 from co-founder Lea Petrášová. He comes from technology and consulting: he worked in the Salesforce ecosystem, then co-founded Bluez and helped it grow until Rockaway Group acquired it. At Vexl he focuses on the user experience, global growth, and markets where people actually use bitcoin.
people.lea.bio: Lea is a co-founder of Vexl. She cares deeply about privacy and security in the digital world and is an active member of the local cypherpunk community. She wants to make bitcoin easier to use, put privacy first, and keep bitcoin peer-to-peer, as it was meant to be.
people.slush.bio: Marek Palatinus, also known as Slush, co-founded SatoshiLabs and Trezor, the first hardware wallet. He is also a co-founder and advisor at Vexl. A Bitcoin pioneer, he founded Slush Pool, the world's first bitcoin mining pool, and he keeps driving new ideas in the industry.
people.stick.bio: Pavol Rusnák, also known as Stick, is a co-founder and advisor at Vexl. He also co-founded SatoshiLabs and Trezor, the first hardware wallet, where he is a core developer. A cypherpunk and a tireless worker in the Bitcoin space, he believes open-source software and hardware protect people's power and independence.
people.josef.bio: Josef Tětek leads Trezor Academy, a non-profit education program that helps people around the world start using bitcoin. He has a long-standing interest in Bitcoin, Austrian economics, and political philosophy. In 2010 he founded the Czech and Slovak Ludwig von Mises Institute, and he wrote the book Bitcoin: Separation of Money and State.

press.statement.title: Vexl statement
press.statement.p1: Vexl is a groundbreaking mobile app that is changing the way users buy and sell bitcoin (BTC) by combining the best aspects of decentralized exchanges, social marketplaces, and dating sites.
press.statement.p2: Vexl launched in 2022, and since then our mission has been to provide a simple, inclusive, secure, and private platform for peer-to-peer bitcoin trades without KYC.
press.statement.p3: Our unique approach emphasizes trust and reputation. Vexl lets users interact not only with their direct contacts but also with their extended network, which builds trust and good behavior in the marketplace. This creates a more trusted and engaging community for everyone.
press.statement.p4: At Vexl, we put user privacy and control first, so our users have full power over their identity based on their preferences and threat model. We keep the platform secure by having no access to any information about users' activities or identities, which sets us apart from traditional platforms.
press.statement.p5: Experience the future of buying and selling bitcoin with the Vexl app, where trust, privacy, and human-driven control come together in an inclusive experience for everyone. Join us and become part of a more connected and trusted Bitcoin community.

journey.origins.title: Born inside SatoshiLabs
journey.origins.text: Product research starts inside SatoshiLabs in 2021: a way to buy and sell bitcoin without KYC, with people you actually know. The first native iOS and Android apps are built in early 2022, Vexl s.r.o. is founded in June, and Citadelo audits the apps in August.
journey.chaincamp.title: Public debut at ChainCamp
journey.chaincamp.text: Vexl launches publicly at ChainCamp in Ostrava, Czechia. The team's launch goal of 100,000 uploaded contacts is reached within an hour of the presentation.
journey.openSource.title: Open source from the start
journey.openSource.text: Vexl publishes its mobile apps, cryptography library, and backend services on GitHub under the GPL-3.0 license. Anyone can check the code instead of trusting privacy promises.
journey.foundation.title: The Vexl Foundation launches
journey.foundation.text: SatoshiLabs launches the non-profit Vexl Foundation at BTC Prague, with Lea Petrášová as president, together with the Financial Tyranny Index. Vexl becomes a community-funded public good, not a venture-backed startup.
journey.v2.title: Apple blocks Vexl, Vexl 2.0 ships
journey.v2.text: Apple rejects Vexl 2.0 from the App Store, calling in-person cash trades "clearly reckless". Vexl retires version 1.0 on September 9, launches the rewritten Vexl 2.0 worldwide on Android and iOS TestFlight, and opens translations to the community that fall.
journey.opensats.title: First OpenSats grant
journey.opensats.text: OpenSats includes Vexl in its third wave of Bitcoin grants and renews the support in December 2024 and July 2025, $120,000 in total. Grants keep Vexl free to use, with no trading fees and no data collection.
journey.goods.title: Goods, services, and HRF backing
journey.goods.text: Vexl ships the Trade Checklist, opens offers to everyday goods and services, and rewrites its backend in TypeScript. Late in the year it starts a crowdfunding campaign on Geyser and gets a grant from the Human Rights Foundation's Bitcoin Development Fund to strengthen its cryptography and grow communities in Africa.
journey.clubs.title: Vexl Clubs and direct Android downloads
journey.clubs.text: Vexl Clubs let local Bitcoin meetups and groups trade inside trusted circles beyond their phone contacts. From June 9, signed Android APKs come straight from GitHub Releases, and Zapstore support follows two days later, so Android users don't need Google Play.
journey.freedomStore.title: Freedom Store challenges Apple
journey.freedomStore.text: Using the EU's rules for alternative app marketplaces, the Vexl Foundation and AltStore.io launch the Freedom Store at BTC Prague. iPhone users in the EU can install Vexl and other open-source Bitcoin, e-cash, and Nostr apps outside Apple's App Store.
journey.newCeo.title: 17,000 users and a new CEO
journey.newCeo.text: Vexl passes 17,000 users and millions of connections between friends and friends of friends, led by Czechia, Slovakia, and Germany. Viliam Klamarčík becomes CEO to lead global growth, and co-founder Lea Petrášová focuses on long-term strategy and the Foundation.
journey.redesign.title: Faster, redesigned, and free of Google
journey.redesign.text: Offers encrypt up to 250 times faster, the app gets a full redesign in June, and in August Vexl drops Google Maps and Google's notification service. Fall releases add encrypted chat photos, message reactions, step-by-step identity reveals, and "Check with a common friend" before you meet.
